articles.title: WHO Classifies El Niño Health Impacts Emergency, Flags India High Risk
articles.excerpt: WHO's September assessment lists high or very high risks for India from heat, dengue and leptospirosis, with malaria in parts of the northeast, as the WMO says El Niño is expected to reach record strength by December.

Asia Daily — WHO Classifies El Niño Health Impacts as Emergency
The Hindu BusinessLine — Strong El Niño Could Drag Crisis Into 2027

articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with family in India, WHO's assessment names the specific risks to watch by region — heat, dengue and leptospirosis nationally, and malaria in parts of the northeast — and the household precautions that follow from them.

articles.title: Man Dies After Biting Explosive Handed to Him as Rasgulla Sweet
articles.excerpt: Police in Madhya Pradesh's Dindori district say a 35-year-old man died after a crude boar-hunting explosive, described to him as a rasgulla, detonated in his mouth, and two men have been held as officers probe whether it was killing or mischief.
articles.nri_angle: A widely shared India news story with no direct action for diaspora readers; its relevance is the police investigation into crude hunting explosives circulating as ordinary food.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bihar Man Arrested After Wife's Killing in Munger, Police Say He Surrendered
articles.excerpt: Police in Jamalpur say the 55-year-old retired loco pilot surrendered with the couple's two daughters after his 28-year-old wife was found dead at their rented home. The motive remains under investigation.

sources.label: Linda Ikeji's Blog (citing The Times of India)

articles.nri_angle: Domestic-violence cases from home states are followed closely by diaspora families with relatives in Bihar, and the helpline information in this story is included for readers who may need it for family in India.

articles.title: BrahMos Exports Widen in Southeast Asia as Philippines Seeks More Systems
articles.excerpt: The Philippines has taken delivery and Vietnam has signed, while talks with other Southeast Asian nations are at an advanced stage and still await government clearance, reporting says.

articles.title: India Cancels Norwegian Journalist's Visa Hours Before Hyderabad Summit Trip
articles.excerpt: Helle Lyng Svendsen of Dagsavisen says her visa was cancelled minutes before departure for a press-freedom panel. The Editors Guild and CPJ have sought an explanation; the government had not publicly given one as of November 13.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian-origin journalists and readers abroad, the case is a closely watched test of how India handles critical foreign reporting and access for international media.

articles.title: India-EU Free Trade Agreement Will Be Game Changer, Says German Envoy
articles.excerpt: Ambassador Jasper Wieck said the pact, expected to be signed by year-end and take effect in the first half of next year, will cut tariffs and integrate supply chains.
articles.nri_angle: For Indian exporters, professionals and students in Europe, lower tariffs and deeper India-Germany supply-chain ties could open new trade and job opportunities.

articles.image_caption: Modi
articles.nri_angle: For Bengaluru's large diaspora with family in the city, the new Bannerghatta Road corridor offers a faster public-transport link across the congested south of the city.

articles.title: Andhra to Enact Investment Protection Act So Deals Survive Regime Change
articles.excerpt: Naidu told the CII summit that land, incentives and approvals granted to investors will be legally protected from reversal by future governments, with a Bill planned for the December winter session.
articles.nri_angle: For NRI investors, the escrow accounts are already live; the Act, if passed in December, would decide whether Andhra's promises outlast its government.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Andhra Earmarks 5,000 Acres Near Tirupati for Space Sector Push
articles.excerpt: At the CII Partnership Summit's close, Naidu named the Tirupati land bank as rocket startups Agnikul Cosmos and Hathor Rockets signed MoUs worth a proposed Rs 760 crore combined.
articles.image_caption: The Tirumala hills at Tirupati in Andhra Pradesh. The state government has earmarked 5,000 acres near Tirupati for the space sector.
articles.nri_angle: Andhra's space cluster near Tirupati, within reach of Sriharikota, is the state's bid for the private launch industry Indian-origin engineers abroad increasingly work in.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Farm Growth Topped 4% for a Decade, Modi Tells Kisan Tak Conference
articles.excerpt: Addressing the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference in New Delhi, the Prime Minister credited a decade of above-4% farm growth with helping 50 crore people defeat poverty, and urged crop diversification and natural farming.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi. He said farm growth had averaged over 4 percent over the past decade and that 50 crore people had defeated poverty.
articles.nri_angle: Modi's claims frame the farm economy many diaspora families still draw income and land from; the figures are the Prime Minister's, citing a World Bank study, and are reported here as his address stated them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NPPA Orders Strict Checks So Cancer Drug Price Cuts Reach Patients
articles.excerpt: With revised prices for 137 anti-cancer drugs in force since November 9, the drug pricing authority has ordered strict enforcement checks; states including Andhra Pradesh have directed inspections of cancer hospitals and pharmacies.
articles.image_caption: Capsules are piled in a close-up photograph. The NPPA has capped trade margins on 137 anti-cancer drugs and ordered strict checks that the revised prices are charged.
articles.nri_angle: Families in India and relatives abroad who fund treatment can verify the legal price of a cancer medicine on the NPPA's Pharma Sahi Daam app before paying a pharmacy or hospital bill.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 19 Indian Seafarers Safe After Tanker Struck Off UAE Coast
articles.excerpt: All 22 crew of the Liberia-flagged MT Dominica Prosperity were evacuated by the UAE Coast Guard after a projectile hit the tanker's engine room off Mina Saqr on November 11, India's shipping minister said.
articles.nri_angle: Indian nationals crew a large share of Gulf shipping; all 19 Indians aboard this tanker were evacuated unharmed, and India's shipping ministry says it is in contact with the vessel's managers on their welfare.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

Voters can get forms and guidance for additions, deletions and corrections ahead of the December 11, 2026 deadline.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora readers can pass the three camp dates and form guidance to family in Tamil Nadu who need to add, delete or correct a voter entry before December 11.

articles.title: Azam Khan Gets Four Days in ED Custody, Faces Lucknow Questioning Friday
articles.excerpt: A Ghaziabad special court gave the ED four days' custody of Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan, until November 16, 2026, in the money-laundering investigation linked to Jauhar University. Khan is to be brought to Lucknow for questioning.
articles.nri_angle: Developments in a major Uttar Pradesh political and university case, reported with the ED's allegations and Khan's own statement kept distinct.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Draft Electoral Rolls Released in Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi for Checking
articles.excerpt: Tamil Nadu's integrated draft electoral roll is out, with district lists published for Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi. Voters have until December 11, 2026 to verify their details and seek additions, deletions or corrections before the final roll on January 4, 2027.
articles.nri_angle: Family members in Tamil Nadu districts can verify their voter entries during the claims window; diaspora readers with relatives in Cuddalore, Villupuram and Kallakurichi can flag the December 11 deadline to them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India TB Mortality Falls 38 Percent Since 2015, WHO Report Finds
articles.excerpt: The WHO Global Tuberculosis Report 2026, as summarised in a government release, puts India's TB death rate at 18 per lakh in 2025, down from 28 per lakh in 2015, with a 94% treatment success rate.
articles.image_caption: Report
articles.nri_angle: Major India public-health milestone from the WHO global report, relevant to diaspora families with ties to India.

articles.title: Sonam Wangchuk Claims House Arrest as Ladakh Protests Winter Poll Schedule
articles.excerpt: The climate activist says dozens of armed guards surround his Leh residence after demands to postpone the December 4 hill council elections, while police say he was advised to stay home under prohibitory orders.
articles.image_caption: Ladakh
articles.nri_angle: The dispute over Ladakh's winter polls and Wangchuk's confinement is a major governance story for readers in India and the diaspora following the region.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Woman Loses Arm After Alleged Molestation and Push at Naigaon Station; Suspect Arrested
articles.excerpt: A 20-year-old on a Borivali-to-Virar local was allegedly pushed at Naigaon on November 4, fell between coaches and lost her left arm; police arrested a 53-year-old man after a CCTV review.
articles.image_caption: A station board reads Naigaon at Naigaon railway station. A 20-year-old woman was allegedly pushed at the station on November 4 and lost her left arm.
articles.nri_angle: A safety case on Mumbai locals that diaspora readers with family commuting in Mumbai will follow closely.

articles.title: IIT Madras Pravartak Opens Free Online Training for Students in Classes 7-12 and Teachers
articles.excerpt: Free live online cohorts from November 2026 to January 2027 cover AI, electric vehicles and entrepreneurship for students, and career counselling, leadership and classroom management for teachers.

articles.title: More Than Half of India's Fertiliser Never Feeds the Crop, Scientists Tell Kisan Tak Conference
articles.excerpt: Crops absorb only 30-45% of applied nitrogen and as little as 15% of phosphorus, experts told the Delhi agriculture conference — and the remedy they prescribed was balanced nutrition and root-placed urea, not more bags.
articles.image_caption: Fertiliser being applied to farmland. Scientists told the Kisan Tak conference more than half of India's fertiliser never feeds the crop.
articles.nri_angle: Fertiliser inefficiency drives the subsidy bill and food prices in India, and the nitrogen losses are a major source of air and water pollution.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BBC Verify: Delhi's Official Diwali Averages Missed Every Reading Above 1,000 Micrograms
articles.excerpt: Comparing CPCB figures with DPCC station data, BBC Verify found 217 missing hourly observations in the Diwali peak window and station averages less than half the DPCC's — while the CPCB blames older analysers capped at 1,000 micrograms.
articles.nri_angle: The BBC's findings bear on how much trust residents and visiting families can place in Delhi's official AQI during the winter pollution season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Foreign Divorce Cannot End a Marriage Solemnised in India, Supreme Court Rules
articles.excerpt: In the N. Sridhar Reddy case, the court held that a UK decree based on irretrievable breakdown fails Section 13 CPC, so the husband's bigamy trial continues — while proceedings against his parents and second wife were quashed.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs married in India who divorce abroad on grounds like irretrievable breakdown remain married under Indian law and risk bigamy prosecution if they remarry without a recognised decree.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Kejriwal, Daughter Threatened in Call Demanding Rs 7 Crore in Bishnoi Gang's Name
articles.excerpt: The threat reached AAP MLA Jarnail Singh, who complained to Mohali Police on November 6. A case is registered, but the caller's claimed gang link is unverified.
articles.image_caption: Arvind Kejriwal addresses a press conference in front of an Aam Aadmi Party backdrop. Mohali Police have registered a case after a caller claiming Bishnoi gang membership demanded Rs 7 crore and threatened Kejriwal and his daughter.
articles.nri_angle: Kejriwal leads the AAP, a party with deep support in Punjab and among the Punjabi diaspora; an extortion threat invoking the Bishnoi gang touches a diaspora community that follows Punjab security news closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi to Deliver Plenary Address at Kisan Tak Agriculture Conference in Delhi
articles.excerpt: Around 2,000 farmers are expected at the two-day Bharat Mandapam conference on smart farming, AI and climate-resilient crops, held under the theme 'Smart Kisan, Viksit Bharat.'
articles.image_caption: The poster for the Kisan Tak Bharat Agriculture Conference 2026, presented by Mahindra Tractors. Prime Minister Narendra Modi will deliver the plenary address at the two-day conference at Bharat Mandapam in New Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: Many NRI families retain farmland and farming relatives in India; the conference sets the official direction on farm technology, incomes and agri-exports.

articles.excerpt: The Supreme Court allowed certified green crackers in short windows this Diwali. The science says they pollute less, not nothing — and Delhi's AQI still crossed 350 on Monday morning.

sources.label: Press Association via Chelmsford City News

articles.nri_angle: Diaspora families celebrating Diwali abroad follow the same green-cracker debate as Indian cities weigh tradition against severe winter air.

articles.title: India Bans Export of Lithium-Ion Battery Black Mass With Immediate Effect
articles.excerpt: The Directorate General of Foreign Trade has changed the export status of lithium-ion battery black mass from 'Free' to 'Prohibited' with immediate effect, keeping the mineral-rich recycling material at home for India's battery and electric-vehicle supply chain.
articles.image_caption: Lithium-ion battery packs move along a production line. India has prohibited the export of lithium-ion battery black mass with immediate effect to keep the material for domestic processing.
articles.nri_angle: Keeping black mass at home affects the cost and availability of batteries across India's EV supply chain, which diaspora readers follow through India's auto and clean-energy industries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Air India Losses More Than Double to Rs 22,238 Crore as Expansion Plan Meets Its Bill
articles.excerpt: Air India and Air India Express lost Rs 22,238 crore in the year ended March 2026, up from Rs 10,859 crore a year earlier, even as new CEO Tewolde Gebremariam seeks more widebody aircraft and Tata Sons weighs a capital infusion of more than Rs 10,000 crore.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora travellers, Air India's hub plans for Mumbai, Delhi and Bengaluru and the pace of its widebody expansion shape the nonstop options between India and North America and Europe.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cabinet Approves Rs 62,370 Crore Fertiliser Subsidy for Rabi Season, DAP Price Held
articles.excerpt: The Union Cabinet has approved Nutrient Based Subsidy rates for phosphatic and potassic fertilisers for Rabi 2026-27 with a tentative outlay of Rs 62,370.02 crore, up nearly 64% on the previous Rabi season, while holding the retail price of a 50 kg DAP bag at Rs 1,350.
articles.image_caption: A farmer broadcasts fertiliser by hand over a green field. The Cabinet has approved Rs 62,370 crore in P&K fertiliser subsidy for Rabi 2026-27 while holding the DAP bag price at Rs 1,350.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with farming families in India, the held DAP price of Rs 1,350 per 50 kg bag is the figure that reaches the farm gate this Rabi season.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CPCB Says Diwali Data Gaps Came From Older Monitors' 1,000-Microgram Ceiling
articles.excerpt: In an 11-point clarification issued Tuesday, the Central Pollution Control Board said hourly readings above the calibrated range of its older particulate analysers were automatically treated as errors and dropped from Delhi's averages — and rejected allegations of under-reporting.
articles.image_caption: CPCB
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers with family in Delhi, the clarification explains why official AQI figures relatives rely on for health decisions can fall silent precisely when the air is at its worst.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BJP Wins 77 Tripura Civic Seats Unopposed as Opposition Alleges Intimidation
articles.excerpt: The State Election Commission declared 77 BJP candidates elected unopposed after the withdrawal of nominations closed, leaving 268 of the state's 345 urban local body seats to be contested on November 27.
articles.image_caption: Tripura
articles.nri_angle: Tripura's civic outcome shapes local governance in a state many diaspora families hail from, and the unopposed wins will frame the fairness debate around the November 27 vote.

articles.image_caption: Air India
articles.nri_angle: Kolkata-Mumbai is a busy domestic trunk route used by international passengers connecting through both hubs, so Wednesday's disruption affects onward travel plans well beyond the one flight.

articles.title: India Hits 98.4% Immunisation Coverage, Yet Gaps Leave Millions Missing Shots
articles.excerpt: Full coverage rose from 62% in 2015 to 98.4% in January 2026 and zero-dose children nearly halved, but migration, hesitation, regional gaps and low adult uptake still leave many unprotected.
articles.image_caption: Immunisation
articles.nri_angle: Explains for diaspora families why a portable record such as U-WIN matters when children move between cities or countries, even as India's headline coverage reaches 98.4%.

articles.nri_angle: Lets diaspora readers track the forecast for family districts — snow in Kashmir around Nov 12-13, heavy rain in Tamil Nadu and Kerala on Nov 15-16, and no rain for Delhi till Nov 15.

articles.title: FICCI Puts Air Pollution's Annual Cost at $95 Billion, Urges Health-Led Plan
articles.excerpt: A FICCI-EY paper links polluted air to more than two million deaths in India in 2023 and calls for explicit PM2.5 targets, regional airshed action and year-round health planning instead of seasonal emergency responses.
articles.image_caption: Satellite view of air pollution over northern India (NESDIS). A FICCI report put air pollution's annual cost to India at $95 billion and urged a health-led plan.
articles.nri_angle: Pollution on this scale shapes winter travel, family health and caregiving decisions for diaspora readers with parents and children in India.

articles.title: Three Workers Die After Inhaling Toxic Gas at Tata's Hosur iPhone Plant
articles.excerpt: The contract workers were cleaning a nano-filtration tank at the Hosur plant's effluent treatment plant late on Monday. Apple, Tata Electronics and Tamil Nadu authorities will investigate, as officials say proper safety measures were not in place.
articles.nri_angle: The Hosur plant is a key node in Apple's India iPhone supply chain, which Tata now anchors with roughly 40 percent of Indian iPhone assembly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Mumbai Doctors Warn Oral Cancer Is Striking Patients in Their Late 20s
articles.excerpt: Jaslok's Dr Mehul Bansali links the younger cases to tobacco and gutkha habits beginning at 12-15 — and gives the 2-3 week rule for a mouth ulcer that will not heal.
articles.nri_angle: The actionable rule travels: a mouth ulcer that has not healed in 2-3 weeks needs a specialist and a biopsy decision, wherever you live — early-stage oral cancer is far more survivable than late-stage.

articles.title: Doctors List Early Lung Cancer Warning Signs People Keep Overlooking
articles.excerpt: A cough past three weeks, blood in sputum, repeated chest infections and unexplained weight loss should be checked, not waited out, oncologists and pulmonologists say.

articles.nri_angle: US-based readers get the exact CDC low-dose CT screening criteria — age 50 to 80 and a 20 pack-year smoking history — alongside the symptom thresholds Indian specialists cite.

articles.title: 'Surprised We Are Still Alive': AIIMS Doctor Warns Delhi Air Is Poisonous
articles.excerpt: AIIMS professor Vijay Hadda says even healthy colleagues cannot shake throat irritation from Delhi's post-Diwali air, and that green crackers cut emissions by only about 30 per cent.

articles.title: Chennai Air Worsens Sharply on Diwali as Four Areas Cross AQI 300

articles.nri_angle: Chennai is a top origin and destination city for diaspora travel during the festival season, and post-Diwali air quality shapes return-trip health planning for visiting families.

articles.title: Six of a Family Killed in Fire at Home Above Grocery Store in Maharashtra

articles.title: Delhi Wakes to Post-Diwali Smog as AQI Hits 368, 15 Areas Turn Severe
articles.excerpt: A day after Diwali, every one of Delhi's 54 monitoring stations read above 200, 15 crossed into the severe band, and PM2.5 near Akshardham peaked at more than 50 times the WHO daily limit late on Sunday night.
articles.image_caption: The sun appears as a pale disc through smog over Delhi's skyline, with buildings fading into haze. Delhi's AQI was 368 at 7 a.m. on Monday, a day after Diwali, with 15 areas in the severe category.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with family in Delhi, Monday's readings are the practical test of the visit-and-health advice issued before Diwali: the air stayed in the very poor to severe band across the whole city, not just in hotspots.

articles.title: Wisconsin Infant Dies of Measles, State's First Such Death Since 1990
articles.excerpt: The infant, in southwestern Wisconsin, was linked to an outbreak that has reached 431 cases in 13 counties — the state's highest count in more than 35 years, health officials said.
articles.image_caption: This is the skin of a patient after 3 days of measles infection; treated at the New York - Presbyterian Hospital. An infant in southwestern Wisconsin has died of measles, the first such death reported in the state since 1990, the Wisconsin Department of Health Services said on November 5; the coroner listed measles as the immediate cause of death.
articles.image_credit: Photo: Photo Credit: Content Providers(s): CDC/Dr. Heinz F. Eichenwald via Wikimedia Commons (Public domain)
articles.nri_angle: For families travelling between the US and India, the outbreak is a reminder to check MMR records before travel — infants too young for the standard schedule depend on the immunity of everyone around them.

articles.title: Kanpur Roof Collapse Kills Three of Family, Including Newborn Son
articles.excerpt: A woman, her 21-day-old son and her mother-in-law died after a house roof collapsed in Kanpur's Panki Padao area on Sunday morning, police said. The cause has not been officially stated.
articles.image_caption: Kanpur
articles.nri_angle: A family tragedy in Kanpur that underscores housing-safety concerns many diaspora families share for relatives in older homes in India.

articles.title: Modi Pens Tribute as L.K. Advani Turns 99 and Enters His 100th Year
articles.excerpt: Prime Minister Narendra Modi marked Lal Krishna Advani's 99th birthday — which falls on Diwali this year — with a signed article praising the BJP co-founder's political acumen, while party leaders held a puja and havan at BJP headquarters in New Delhi.
articles.image_caption: L.K. Advani with Prime Minister Narendra Modi during a recent meeting in New Delhi. Modi published a signed tribute article on November 8 as the BJP co-founder turned 99 and entered his 100th year.
articles.nri_angle: Advani shaped the BJP that much of the diaspora grew up watching from afar; his 100th year is a milestone in modern Indian political history.

articles.excerpt: Sirens over Zar'it and Shomera along the Lebanese border were a false identification, the IDF said, weeks after the flydubai FZ1073 incident prompted tighter airline crew screening.
articles.nri_angle: The background flydubai incident involved Indian captain Smit Machchhar, whose actions were honoured by the UAE, a detail of direct interest to Indian readers following aviation security.

articles.title: India's Clean Energy Push Could Cut Fuel Import Bill by $240 Billion, IEA Says
articles.excerpt: The IEA projects cumulative coal and gas import savings approaching $240 billion by 2030, up from more than $100 billion already saved between 2011 and 2025, if fuel prices hold near 2024-25 levels.
articles.image_caption: The graphic describes energy employment in fossil fuel and clean energy sectors, all figures used being estimates. India's clean energy push could cut its cumulative coal and natural gas import bill by nearly $240 billion by 2030, the International Energy Agency said in its India Renewable Energy Market Report 2026, according to reports of the study.
articles.image_credit: Photo: International Energy Agency via Wikimedia Commons (CC BY 4.0)
articles.nri_angle: India's renewable expansion is an energy-security and foreign-exchange story, cutting exposure to imported coal and gas prices.

articles.title: Instagram Offers Creators Up to $500,000 for Videos Without YouTube-Style Revenue Share
articles.excerpt: Meta is funding invited creators to seed Features, its 90-minute video format, but has no advertising revenue share to offer the wider creator community yet.
articles.nri_angle: Indian and diaspora podcasters and comedians earn predictable income from YouTube's revenue share; Features offers them reach and invite-only deals, but no open per-view income yet.

articles.title: Debutant Aniesh Performed Every Action Scene Without a Dupe, Venky Kudumula Says
articles.excerpt: The producer says the newcomer did his own stunts in Itlu Arjuna, the mute-protagonist thriller presented by Nagarjuna and opening November 13.
articles.image_caption: The trailer poster for the Telugu film Itlu Arjuna, featuring debutant Aniesh, ahead of its November 13 theatrical release. Producer Venky Kudumula said Aniesh performed all his action scenes without a dupe.
articles.nri_angle: A Telugu debut built around a mute protagonist, backed by Nagarjuna and Jr NTR, is the kind of word-of-mouth release diaspora audiences track ahead of its November 13 opening.

articles.title: RJD MP Sanjay Yadav Asks President to Act Against DU Professor Sangeet Ragi
articles.excerpt: In a three-page letter dated November 6, Rajya Sabha member Sanjay Yadav asked President Droupadi Murmu, as Visitor of Delhi University, for an impartial inquiry into allegedly caste-based derogatory remarks by Professor Sangeet Ragi in a televised debate.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora readers who studied at Delhi University or follow caste and campus politics from abroad, the case tests how India's central universities handle televised conduct by senior faculty.

articles.title: Farmer Collecting Cattle Fodder Mauled to Death by Tiger in Beed, Maharashtra
articles.excerpt: Devidas (Mahadev) Takle of Deolali village in Ashti tehsil was killed on Saturday while collecting fodder for his cattle in drought-hit Maharashtra, in an attack reports link to a young male tiger camera-trapped in the area on November 2.
articles.image_caption: A Bengal tiger in a file photograph. A farmer collecting cattle fodder was mauled to death by a tiger in Maharashtra's Beed district.
articles.nri_angle: Human-wildlife conflict on farmland fringes is a recurring risk for families across Marathwada; the forest department's advisory and increased patrols are the actionable facts for anyone with family in Beed district.

articles.image_caption: Rachel Apa points to her name on the New York City Marathon entrants wall while holding her race bib, number 29977. Apa collapsed at Mile 24 of the November 1, 2026 race and died later that day.

articles.title: Army Says Claim of 50-km Chinese Advance in Arunachal Is False
articles.excerpt: The Indian Army's fact-check handle named six X accounts it called suspected Pakistan-sponsored handles that circulated the same claim between November 6 and 7, and urged people to verify border claims with official sources.
articles.nri_angle: Border disinformation spreads fast in diaspora WhatsApp and X feeds; the Army's named-account fact-check gives readers a concrete way to check the next viral border claim before forwarding it.

articles.title: How Telangana Got Back 550 Acres in Miyapur Worth About Rs 50,000 Crore
articles.excerpt: A Supreme Court verdict ended the dispute over Miyapur's survey numbers 100 and 101 in the state's favour. The Hindu's explainer traces how the land was claimed, and Chief Minister Revanth Reddy says recovered land worth Rs 1.5 lakh crore has been protected across seven sites.
articles.image_caption: Traffic at Allwyn Cross Roads in Miyapur, Hyderabad. The Supreme Court has ruled that 550 acres of government land in Miyapur belong to the Telangana government.
articles.nri_angle: Hyderabad land values are a live concern for NRI property holders in Telangana; a Supreme Court ruling that 550 acres of Miyapur poramboke land was always the state's — and allegations that the Dharani records portal was manipulated — bear directly on how safely land records can be trusted.

articles.title: Deepavali 2026: Green Crackers Allowed In Delhi-NCR In Two Daily Slots
articles.excerpt: The Supreme Court permitted CSIR-NEERI-certified green crackers on November 7 and 8 between 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. in Delhi-NCR only, with 300-metre no-cracker zones and the full ban returning November 9.
articles.image_caption: Deepavali
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families with homes or relatives in Delhi-NCR, the order sets the only lawful celebration windows this Deepavali — certified green crackers, 6-7 a.m. and 8-10 p.m. on November 7-8 — and does not extend to other Indian states or cities.
